BIOE 5520 — Bioengineering Design for Robotic Rehabilitation | prerequisites, offerings, professors (Northeastern)

NU Map is an independent, student-built planner — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data comes from the public catalog on a schedule; confirm with the official catalog and an advisor. Data updated Aug 2026 · page generated 2026-08-04.

4 semester hoursGraduateLectureusually offered: falltypical days: M/WBostonTraditional

Covers the intersection of robotics, physical therapy, rehabilitation, and movement sciences. Students engage in hands-on projects derived from real-world challenges in collaboration with clinical experts. Follows a systematic design process, from conceptualization to prototype development, emphasizing the application of robotics to enhance therapeutic and rehabilitative outcomes. Key topics include biomechanics, motor control and learning, and sensor integration. Emphasizes collaborative teamwork with peers, faculty, and clinical professionals. Concludes with a project presentation demonstrating functional prototypes to address specific needs in rehabilitation.
